boundaries: the worker -> ffmpeg and ffprobe: the argv that measures a clip, samples it and makes its poster
the worker -> object storage: a second object per clip, under a key nothing else knows
the worker -> Postgres: width, height, duration and thumbnail_url through a hand-written column list
a database row -> a storage key: a value read back out of the database and used to address storage
the handlers -> the browser: the asset JSON, and two new routes that return bytes
the publication access gate -> two queries that must answer the same question
the React media view -> the API: which endpoint each mode calls, and how much it costs to draw a page
stored object -> a local file, whose NAME is read by ffmpeg and by the thumbnail service

instruments.evidence: Four commits since the last ledger's final pass: 1e1acb6b0 (clip frame review, hidden negative prompt), a85e4fdac (measure the clip, store a poster), cf87db741 (reduce the clip for playback), 68b74a58a (a gallery tile shows the poster). 18 files. Boundaries: worker->ffmpeg/ffprobe argv; worker->object storage (a second object per clip); worker->Postgres (width, height, duration, thumbnail_url through a hand-written column list); handler->browser (the asset JSON and two new binary routes); a database row->a storage key; the React component->which endpoint each mode calls.

Read all nine prior ledgers. 390b0e4c R2 (a hand-written decoder ignores struct tags) and R4 (one rule as prose in five places) both bear directly on this change and both recurred here: see poster-R2. 982264d4 video-R4 and instrument C6 governed the untyped-map reads that this change does not use.

The assembled ffmpeg and ffprobe argv are the payloads this change builds. Printed and run for two materially different inputs: portrait 1440x2528 (the real MiniMax render) and 64x64 and 640x480 test clips. The 2K case scaled to 1080x1896; the small case took the no-rendition branch.

Rendered the tile for four states and read the markup: a clip with a poster, a clip with none, an opened clip, and an image. Found the poster img carries the prompt as alt while the button's aria-label overrides it for the accessible name -- an improvement on the previous state (a bare video element with no name), so recorded rather than filed. Also confirmed object-contain, so a portrait frame in a 4:5 tile is not cropped.

Printed the decorated asset JSON for a clip with a poster, a clip without, and an image, and the poster route's status, headers and body for a hit and a miss. thumbnail_url appears only for a clip that has one; the storage URL never appears. Observed but not filed: the poster route sends Cache-Control private, no-store, copied from the clip route, and the browser fetch also passes cache: no-store -- so a gallery re-fetches every poster on every visit. At ~118 KB a tile that is 1.4 MB per visit against the 40 MB the change removed, so it is an optimisation and not a defect. Reported to the user.

Wrote a throwaway against the real Postgres: inserted a media_files row with thumbnail_url, read it back through GetMediaAssetOwned, then deleted the asset and printed the deletion queue. thumbnail_url, width, height and duration all round-tripped. The deletion queue held only the clip -- poster-R1.

The poster is produced by ffmpeg from a real 6.62 MB MiniMax render, and the frame was extracted and looked at, not merely measured: 640x1124, a representative full-body frame, correct as a tile. The playback rendition was run on the same real clip (6.62 MB -> 2.21 MB, 1080x1896, audio preserved) and both files were sent to the user side by side. No model-facing prompt changed in these four commits, so there is no unrendered prompt change to declare.

The poster key is written in one place (video_clip_probe.go) and read in two (the private route, the deletion). They did not agree on the shape: IsOmniChatGeneratedStoragePath requires a bare uuid stem and the poster's stem is '<job id>-poster' -- poster-R2.
The frontend reads asset.thumbnail_url; the backend sets it in decorateOmniChatAsset for the private path. On the public path the field did not exist on either side -- poster-R4.

The generated-storage-path rule existed twice: models.IsOmniChatGeneratedStoragePath and a weaker local copy in the handler. Ran both against the same inputs; they disagreed on segment count and on a non-numeric owner -- poster-R2.

instruments.why: No provider or worker contract changed. The OpenRouter video request and the RunPod worker are untouched by these four commits.

instruments.evidence: thumbnail_url crosses two hand-written boundaries. The private path's omniChatAssetSelect and scanOmniChatMediaAsset already carried it, proved by a real-database round trip. No untyped-map or reflection accessor was added. The nearest equivalent is the poster key read out of a database row and used to address storage; it is exercised through the real accessor in both directions -- written by the worker, read back by the route and by the deletion.
OmniChatPosterStorageKey accepts what the worker actually writes: /uploads/omnichat/generated/<owner>/<job id>-poster.jpg, asserted with a real uuid rather than a literal.

Thirteen hostile inputs against the poster key rule: traversal, too few segments, too many segments, a non-numeric owner, another owner, a doubled slash, a backslash, another prefix, the clip itself, a non-poster jpg, a stem that is not a job, an absolute host, whitespace. All refused.

Boundaries on the same rule: empty string, whitespace only, a nil thumbnail, owner id zero and negative. Boundaries on playbackScale: exactly at the cap, one over, zero, and odd dimensions that must round to even.

Compared the poster routes against the media routes beside them, field by field: ownership or publication gate, scan status, storage nil, size cap before download, Content-Length, nosniff, and the viewer-scoped cache headers with Vary. Then compared the two grids -- the gallery got the poster and the explore feed did not, which is poster-R4.

Every branch reachable: the no-rendition branch by a clip inside the cap, the grew-larger branch by a clip that encodes larger, the no-poster tile by every clip that predates a85e4fdac, the placeholder by a clip whose poster fails. expanded on an explore card defaults false and is true only on the detail route, so preview is genuinely on in the feed.

probeClip returns zeros on every failure and said nothing, so a worker with no ffprobe would store every clip with no dimensions in silence -- the original defect in a quieter form. poster-R3. The poster and rendition failures already logged.

The clip review is gated on !job.AllowNSFW; the poster and the measurement are not, which is correct -- both are metadata, not a content decision. The explore poster route carries the same social rate limiter as the explore content route beside it.

Three duplications found. The generated-path rule (poster-R2). The publication access gate, which would have had to be copied to ask the same question for the poster and is now one constant. The omnichat/generated prefix, which existed in four places and is now the models rule plus the two fmt calls that build keys.
